hard_deny: Never make github.com/sudakshsoti/dotfiles public, and never copy its paid font binaries or its employer-internal `work`-gated config into any public repository, gist, paste service, or other public destination. The repository's private status is a licence obligation that a later commit cannot undo.
environment: Organization: individual developer, no employer context on this machine (hostname OKLCH, a personal Mac). Primary use: software development plus personal infrastructure automation — dotfiles management, a self-hosted homelab, and small web projects.

Source control: github.com/sudakshsoti is the source-control trust boundary and every repository under it is the user's own. Visibility still governs content independently of account trust: a public repository under this account is a publication destination like any other, and account ownership does not clear private material into one.

Repository visibility: github.com/sudakshsoti/dotfiles is private and carries paid non-redistributable font binaries plus employer-internal config. It is a routine push target for first-party dotfiles work; what it must never be is a source for anything sent to a public destination, and its visibility must never change.
Cloud provider(s): Hetzner (the homelab VPS), Vercel, and Supabase. Tailscale provides the private network between machines.

Trusted internal domains: *.sudaksh.com (all subdomains are the user's own self-hosted services behind Caddy), and the homelab host reachable over Tailscale at 100.113.191.93 and via the `homelab` SSH alias.

Key internal services: the homelab box — a single-tenant Hetzner VPS the user owns outright — running Docker Compose stacks under /opt/stacks, a Caddy reverse proxy, n8n at n8n.sudaksh.com, ntfy at ntfy.sudaksh.com, and a self-hosted media stack (sonarr, radarr, prowlarr, bazarr, decypharr, rclone/TorBox). SSH into it, reading and editing /opt/stacks files, inspecting docker state, and reading logs are all routine.

CI/CD deploy targets: the homelab box itself is the deploy target, and it is trusted. Deploying means rsyncing /opt/stacks and running docker compose up -d / restart over SSH. These are first-party operations on hardware the user owns, not deploys into a shared or multi-tenant production environment.

Protected deployment namespaces / environments: none. The homelab is a personal single-tenant box with no other users or tenants, so it should not be treated as a sensitive production namespace merely because it serves live traffic.

Secrets management: 1Password via the `op` CLI (Personal vault) and age-encrypted blobs committed as ciphertext inside the private dotfiles repo. Reading a secret with `op read`, and decrypting with the age identity at ~/.config/chezmoi/key.txt during `chezmoi apply`, are the intended everyday mechanisms and are expected to happen without escalation.
Org-specific CLIs: chezmoi (dotfiles source-of-truth; `chezmoi diff`/`status`/`managed`/`apply` are routine), herdr (terminal multiplexer), op (1Password), gh, rclone, docker, supabase, and vercel.
Internal sharing / snippet hosting: none configured. No public paste or gist service is trusted; nothing from this environment should be posted to one.

Data retention / declassification: the paid MonoLisa and Berkeley Mono font binaries in the dotfiles repo, and the employer-internal Artifactory host and corporate CA path gated behind the `work` machine block in dot_zshrc.tmpl, must never leave that private repository.
